mandate.objective: Admit the initial US IT Services research constitution, one industry Thesis and the Accenture company Thesis under human gate.

drivers.label: Bookings mix and conversion
drivers.mechanism: Consulting and managed-services bookings convert into revenue on different schedules, so mix and conversion determine forward growth visibility.

drivers.label: AI and reinvention demand
drivers.mechanism: Client spending on data, cloud and generative-AI programs expands the addressable transformation budget and can create follow-on managed-services work.

drivers.label: Delivery economics
drivers.mechanism: Utilization, workforce mix, pricing and productivity determine whether revenue growth becomes operating profit growth.

drivers.label: Cash conversion and capital return
drivers.mechanism: Working-capital discipline converts earnings into free cash flow that can fund buybacks and dividends.

metric_specs.label: Total new bookings
metric_specs.definition: Total contract value recorded as new bookings during the period.
caveats: Booking definitions and cancellation assumptions can differ across issuers.

metric_specs.label: Consulting new bookings
metric_specs.definition: New bookings attributed to consulting services during the period.
caveats: Consulting work is generally shorter-cycle and more exposed to discretionary client spending.

metric_specs.label: Managed services new bookings
metric_specs.definition: New bookings attributed to managed services during the period.
caveats: Managed-services contracts are longer-cycle and may convert into revenue gradually.

metric_specs.label: Revenue growth in local currency
metric_specs.definition: Year-over-year revenue growth excluding foreign-exchange translation effects under the issuer's reported definition.
caveats: Local-currency growth is a management-defined measure and must be reconciled to reported revenue.

metric_specs.label: Generative AI bookings
metric_specs.definition: Bookings management attributes to generative-AI work under its disclosed classification.
caveats: Management classification can change and may overlap with cloud, data or reinvention work.

metric_specs.label: Generative AI revenue
metric_specs.definition: Revenue management attributes to generative-AI work under its disclosed classification.
caveats: This is a management-defined subset and is not a standardized accounting segment.

metric_specs.label: Adjusted operating margin
metric_specs.definition: Adjusted operating income divided by revenue under the issuer's reconciliation.
caveats: Adjustments must be reconciled to GAAP operating income and compared consistently over time.

metric_specs.label: Workforce utilization
metric_specs.definition: Billable utilization under the issuer's disclosed workforce definition.
caveats: Population and methodology must be checked before comparing across companies.

metric_specs.label: Voluntary attrition
metric_specs.definition: Trailing or period voluntary employee attrition under the issuer's disclosed definition.
caveats: The time window and employee population must be retained with the observation.

metric_specs.label: Workforce
metric_specs.definition: Period-end employee count under the issuer's disclosed definition.
caveats: Acquisitions, contractors and workforce reclassification can affect comparability.

metric_specs.label: Free cash flow
metric_specs.definition: Operating cash flow less capital expenditures under the issuer's reconciliation.
caveats: Seasonality and acquisition-related cash flows must be separated where disclosed.

metric_specs.label: Free cash flow conversion
metric_specs.definition: Free cash flow divided by the explicitly stated earnings denominator for the same period.
caveats: The earnings denominator and period must be retained; quarterly conversion is seasonally noisy.

metric_specs.label: Share repurchases
metric_specs.definition: Cash spent on common-share repurchases during the period.
caveats: Gross repurchases should not be confused with net share-count reduction.

driver_packs.title: US IT Services Driver Pack v1

thesis_templates.statement: AI and reinvention demand plus managed services can offset weak discretionary consulting and sustain profitable growth.
thesis_templates.mechanism: AI-led programs create consulting work and follow-on managed-services demand; bookings conversion drives revenue while delivery productivity protects operating margin.
thesis_templates.implied_expectation: AI and total bookings convert into mid-single-digit local-currency revenue growth without material operating-margin dilution.

driver_packs.title: US IT Services Driver Pack v2

thesis_templates.statement: AI and reinvention demand plus managed services can offset weak discretionary consulting and sustain profitable growth.
thesis_templates.mechanism: AI-led programs create consulting work and follow-on managed-services demand; bookings conversion drives revenue while delivery productivity protects operating margin.
thesis_templates.implied_expectation: AI and total bookings convert into mid-single-digit local-currency revenue growth without material operating-margin dilution.

thesis_templates.statement: US IT services demand is bottoming: discretionary consulting declines decelerate while AI-led reinvention bookings and managed-services conversion stabilize aggregate industry growth.
thesis_templates.mechanism: New bookings lead revenue by two to four quarters; when the bookings mix shifts toward managed services and AI-led reinvention while discretionary consulting declines decelerate, aggregate revenue growth stops decelerating and inflects to a low-single-digit recovery.
thesis_templates.implied_expectation: Aggregate US IT services revenue growth stops decelerating within two to four quarters of the bookings inflection and stabilizes at a low-single-digit rate.

doctrine_pack.title: US IT Services Research Doctrine v1

lenses.label: Demand inflection
lenses.objective: Detect whether US IT services demand is bottoming by tracking bookings mix, conversion and AI-led reinvention demand ahead of reported revenue.

constitution.title: US IT Services Research Constitution v1

question_admission: A question is worth researching only if a verified answer would change a Thesis, a driver view or the weekly brief; before admission, state which one it changes and in which direction.
Information gain is the distance between the plausible answer distribution before and after the probe; if every outcome leaves the current view unchanged, the question is not admitted.
Prefer questions whose answers generalize across the coverage universe over single-company curiosities, unless the company is an explicit coverage anchor.
The standing question 'has US IT services demand bottomed' stays open until its falsifiers or confirmations resolve the inflection; do not fork into unrelated themes.
causal_chain: Enterprise IT budgets are approved annually and re-allocated quarterly, so discretionary consulting spend reacts to macro confidence with a one-to-two-quarter lag.
New bookings lead revenue by two to four quarters: bookings mix and conversion determine forward revenue visibility before it appears in reported growth.
AI-led reinvention programs create a new budget pool that can offset discretionary consulting weakness and generate follow-on managed-services work.
Managed-services contracts convert annuity-style and damp revenue volatility, so their share of bookings stabilizes aggregate growth.
Delivery economics (utilization, workforce mix, pricing, productivity) transmit demand into operating margin; a demand bottom without margin stability is not a profit inflection.
Cash conversion and capital return are trailing confirmations, not demand signals; they cannot lead the inflection call.

hierarchy: SEC filings (10-Q, 10-K, 8-K exhibits) are the primary numeric authority; only same-filing comparisons are admissible.
Company earnings releases sit below SEC filings for numbers but above transcripts for management-defined metrics such as bookings and local-currency growth.
Authenticated earnings-call transcripts are the primary semantic authority for management framing; transcript numbers never override filings.
Management-defined classifications (GenAI bookings, reinvention) must retain their disclosed definition and caveats with every observation.
conflict_adjudication: A GAAP filing number always overrides a transcript or press-release restatement of the same metric.
Local-currency growth must be reconciled to reported revenue before use; unreconciled management measures are recorded as caveats, not as claims.
When two issuers' metrics conflict on the same driver, record the definitional difference as a debate instead of averaging.
Quarterly observations must bind the exact period, currency and unit; cross-period or cross-unit comparison is a definitional error.

required_falsifier_searches: Each weekly cycle must actively search for evidence that the demand-bottoming call is wrong, starting with aggregate bookings contraction extending two or more consecutive quarters.
Search for AI-led reinvention bookings failing to convert into revenue within two to four quarters.
Search for managed-services renewal or backlog deterioration at the largest coverage-universe issuers.
Search for pricing or margin sacrifice accompanying any growth stabilization.
alternative_explanations: Foreign-exchange translation effects masquerading as local-currency inflection.
Inorganic growth from acquisitions inflating reported revenue.
One-off large deal wins distorting a single quarter's bookings.
Accounting reclassification or definition changes in bookings or GenAI classifications.

materiality: Every driver observation must state its magnitude in revenue-growth percentage points before it can support or weaken a Thesis.
Demand signals must be mapped to earnings through the operating-margin bridge (utilization, pricing, mix) before influencing company Theses.
Company Theses must state the market expectation they differentiate against; a view matching consensus is not an investable Thesis.
Valuation mapping (multiple versus growth trajectory) is recorded alongside Theses but never auto-generated from a Claim.

continue_when: The weekly brief changes any Thesis, driver view or evidence gap.
New SEC filings or earnings calls for coverage-universe issuers arrive with decision-relevant metrics.
A falsifier search returns material new evidence in either direction.
refresh_when: Evidence supporting a current Thesis exceeds its freshness window (latest quarter for numeric claims, thirty days for semantic claims).
A conflict adjudication reopens a previously settled debate.
stop_when: All falsifiers of the industry Thesis have resolved against it, or all have resolved for it and the expectation horizon has passed.
The mandate covering the industry is retired.
escalate_when: A major Thesis change (confidence flip, statement rewrite or falsifier resolution) is proposed; only a human can admit it.
Coverage expansion beyond the current universe, or any budget, permission or connector extension is requested.
Two consecutive cycles produce no new decision-relevant evidence despite executed probes.

criteria: The weekly brief states what changed this week, its impact on existing Theses, company and driver divergence, evidence gaps, key debates, next research questions and source authority.
Every number in an output traces to a formal EvidenceVersion or is explicitly labeled as a candidate.
Thesis status is 'insufficient' unless a formal current ThesisVersion exists; outputs never auto-generate investment conclusions.
A good research output reduces the open question set or sharpens a falsifier; a bad one restates known facts.

content.statement: US IT services demand is approaching a bottom: discretionary consulting declines are decelerating while AI-led reinvention bookings and managed-services conversion build, implying aggregate industry revenue growth inflects from deceleration to a low-single-digit recovery over the next two to four quarters.
content.mechanism: New bookings lead revenue by two to four quarters. A bookings mix shifting toward managed services and AI-led reinvention, alongside decelerating discretionary consulting declines, stabilizes aggregate growth before it recovers.
content.implied_expectation: Aggregate US IT services revenue growth stops decelerating and stabilizes at a low-single-digit rate within two to four quarters of the bookings inflection.
content.change_reason: Initial industry-level admission candidate for the standing question 'has US IT services demand bottomed', bound to the US IT Services driver pack v2 under human gate.

decision.rationale: Isolated canary decision: the industry candidate is bound to the active mandate, driver pack v2, the industry-demand-bottoming template, explicit drivers and falsifiers.

content.statement: Large-scale AI and reinvention work plus managed services can offset soft discretionary consulting, allowing Accenture to sustain mid-single-digit local-currency growth without sacrificing operating margin.
content.mechanism: AI-led programs create consulting work and follow-on managed-services demand; bookings conversion drives revenue while utilization and delivery productivity protect operating margin.
content.implied_expectation: AI and total bookings convert into mid-single-digit local-currency revenue growth while adjusted operating margin remains stable or improves.
content.change_reason: Initial human-reviewed ACN coverage candidate under the US IT Services driver pack v2, admitted alongside the P8a research constitution.

decision.rationale: Isolated canary decision: the ACN candidate is bound to the active mandate, driver pack v2, explicit drivers and falsifiers, and its company ownership feeds the company-to-thesis mapping.
